_source: Balance Bible §37 (per-map tests: high ground, choke width, cover, buildable area, artillery positions). Numbers chosen to sit at or below the armor-facing swing (combat-rules.json armorFacing 0.9/1.1/1.3) so terrain shapes fights without deciding them outright.

highGround._rule: High ground gives a real, symmetric edge — better both on defense (you see them coming, they hit you less) and on offense (your fire reaches farther and lands harder). It is strong but NOT absolute: mass, splash, and flanking from below still break a hilltop, so holding high ground rewards positioning without becoming a hard lock.

shootingDown.vision: full — high ground sees over obstacles and further; the classic scouting perch
shootingDown._note: the OFFENSIVE half: longer reach + harder-hitting fire onto low ground

shootingUp.vision: reduced — the plateau top is hidden until you climb, scout it, or gain elevated vision
shootingUp._note: the DEFENSIVE half: attackers below hit softer, shorter, and half-blind

highGround.netSwing: ~30% effective firepower swing to the holder of the high ground (≈+15% down, ≈−15% up), comparable to a rear-armor hit — meaningful, breakable by numbers.

exemptions.areaWeapons: splash / artillery / flame IGNORE the shooting-up penalty (consistent with combat-rules.json coverNote) — dedicated area fire is how you dislodge a dug-in hilltop
exemptions.shortRangeAndMelee: no elevation modifier — you are already inside the gap
exemptions.artilleryOnHighGround: gains the rangeMult and full vision, making elevated artillery positions a §37 test item

access.ramps: the only ground route onto a plateau — a natural strongpoint and §14 'defensive terrain' comeback tool; narrow ramps concentrate the defender's fire and multiply splash
access.airAndClimbers: aircraft and any climb/jump/teleport unit ignore ramps, so an all-ground army cannot be walled out of every hill

naturalBarriers._rule: Barriers channel movement into readable lanes and create the chokes, flanks, and safe pockets the economy and army-composition rules assume. Every barrier states what it blocks and what bypasses it.

bypassedBy: amphibious / naval where the map allows
impassable.role: define the map skeleton — spawns, expansion pockets, and the chokes between them

forest.blocks: vehicle line-of-sight and vehicle movement; infantry may pass
forest.grants: concealment (see combat-rules.json forestConcealment — reduced enemy detection, no full invisibility while firing)
forest._note: infantry ambush terrain; the Scorch Buggy / Howitzer double as forest-clearers

rubble.blocks: partial — slows movement, gives light cover
rubble.grants: temporary cover; salvageable wreckage (§14 comeback tool)
rubble._note: created by destroyed structures/vehicles; transient, unlike cliffs

chokes._rule: Choke width is a §37 per-map test. Width sets which army the terrain rewards.

narrow.favors: splash / artillery / defensive holds — few units engage the front, area fire is king
narrow.risk: a single splash or a walled ramp can hard-stop a much larger force — pair with a flank route so it is not an auto-hold

medium.favors: standard combined-arms engagements — the default competitive width

wideOpen.favors: mobility, flanking, and vehicles — mass and maneuver over chokepoint splash

perMapTestHooks._note: extends the §37 checklist in design/07-maps.md with the numeric terrain items above
items: every plateau reachable by ground via at least one ramp (no air-only high ground on a ground map)
high-ground artillery positions cannot bombard an enemy base from full safety (elevated range must not out-range the whole approach)
at least one flank around every narrow choke, so terrain rewards but never dictates
spawns not on unequal elevation relative to each other (mirror the high ground)
